$comment: Camera presets. Operators pick a plain-language look; the lens, aperture and focus behind it are hidden. Technical values are PLACEHOLDERS until the team settles the final lenses. The structure is final. Earlier draft values (50mm f/2.8, 35mm f/1.4, 15mm ultra-wide) are in git history, commit 1520fc2.

model_framing.$comment: Field-of-view factor for the proxy handed to the image model. Tried 1.25 to offset Nano Banana 2 drawing objects larger than their shapes; it had no effect (the model sizes the front plate at about 43% of the frame regardless), so it is back to 1 and the prompt states the scale in real-world terms instead (story.ts scaleSentence).

look.$comment: Locked to close-hero (Fernando, 2026-10-07): the Look picker is gone, so the angle is the only camera choice. Earlier table-context (35mm) and wide-scene (15mm) placeholders are in git history. Each preset bundles lens + aperture + focus so users never choose an f-stop. The lens and the film look are stated once by the photodocumentary sentence (story.ts filmSentence, using focal_length_mm), so a final prompt here covers only aperture, focus and food texture.

options.label: Close-up hero
options.help: Tight on the meal and the bottle, the place behind soft but recognizable.
options.texture: Food looks real and freshly made: natural textures, visible char, crumbs, moisture and small imperfections, with soft natural highlights, never glossy, waxy or plastic-looking.

hidden.focus: the front of the main dish; the whole table setting, including the Coca-Cola product, stays sharp; the room behind is soft but recognizable

depth_of_field.$comment: How much of the picture is sharp (Fernando, 2026-10-10, staging). One fixed preset for every scene for now; the structure is a list so it can become a picker later (scene spec camera.depth). Was f/2.0 with rapid fall-off, which left parts of the plate soft and turned the room into a wash. The aperture is named once, then described in words, since image models read f-numbers as style hints. {drinks} is filled in by rules.ts lookSentence. No ISO or shutter speed: they change nothing in a generated image. No foreground props or people: the layout fixes what is on the table, and Phase 1 allows no people.

options.label: Table sharp, room soft
options.help: The whole meal and the bottle sharp, the place behind soft but still recognizable.
options.focus: Moderate depth of field, as at about f/5.6, with focus set on the front of the main dish. The whole table setting is sharp from the near table edge to the far side of the plate: every dish, its garnish and {drinks}, crisp down to the label and the rim.
options.layers: The picture reads in three planes: the near edge of the table in front, the meal and the Coca-Cola product sharp in the middle, and the room behind in a soft, creamy blur that still keeps the recognizable shapes, colors and light of the place, never a featureless wash.

angle.$comment: Pitches set by Fernando on 2026-10-07 (10 / 20 / 40, was 15 / 30 / 45): at 30 degrees the eye line sat far above the frame while Gemini drew the room at standing eye level, so tables looked too steep for their rooms. The angle sentence (rules.ts angleSentence) now states where the eye line falls and asks for the room from the same viewpoint.

recommendations.$comment: Recommended angle by entree, shown on the Camera step and preselected until the operator picks one. Dish words are checked first (whole words, any case, plurals included) against the hero dish and the chosen preparation; the first rule with a matching word wins. When no word matches, the agent's food silhouette (Preparation massClass) and the main vessel (Plating vessel) decide, in rule order. Nothing matching means the default angle.

rules.reason: Tall, layered food reads best from low, nearly at profile, so the camera sees its height and every layer.
Soups, stews and bowls read best from above, looking down into the bowl so the surface, broth and toppings show.
